unit: Department of Economics, Lancaster University Management School
fields_raw: My research interests span a wide range of applied economics/econometrics. She has been working on flexible labour markets in Europe and this has included an examination of the success of the various short-time working schemes (furlough) adopted during the pandemic. Allied work looks at labour market transitions. I also have interests in education and am investigating how successful international aid has been in improving educational attainment, one of the key SDGs. I am also looking at the role of financial development on growth and have been working in a related field looking at foreign direct investment and growth. My interests also cover productivity and emerging economies.

name: Peter Jacko
title: Senior Lecturer
unit: Lancaster University Management School - Management Science
fields_raw: Peter is devoted to the development of methods for the solution of problems in the design and management of complex systems such as health processes, business decision-making, and communications networks. The leading themes of his research are stochastic modelling of real problems and devising tractable and well-performing solutions for efficient allocation of scarce resources over time. His research work benefits from the interaction of mathematics, statistics, computing, and/or economics, typical for the discipline of operational research, and he also has extensive experience in scientific computer programming, including simulation. His main research line recently has been the optimal patient-centric design of modern adaptive clinical trials, which can often be modelled as variants of the multi-armed bandit problem.

name: Dermot O'Reilly
title: Senior Lecturer in Management Learning and Leadership
unit: Lancaster University Management School - Organisation, Work & Technology
fields_raw: My research interests revolve around interpretative and critical perspectives on social and organisational development, co-ordination, and conflict. I have a particular focus on the forms and dynamics of leadership, organizing, and learning. At the core of this intellectual endeavour is an interest in the dynamic and multiply-tendential processes, moments and relations that comprise development, co-ordination, and conflict. In particular, I am interested in the cultural, political, economic, and ecological processes and relations that create, enable, and constrain co-ordination and conflict (for example, in relation to cultural processes – ideation, imaginaries, discourses, social learning, norms and modes of valuing; political processes - domination, legitimation, authority, and dispute; economic processes – reproduction, redistribution, and capitals; and ecological processes - generation, development, contest, synthesis, and decline).

My phenonomenological interests are founded on my work on student approaches to learning in Higher Education.
